WHO ARE WE?

Key Overview:
As a Member of Technical Staff in Post-Training, you will train our large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning and develop methods that help them generalize beyond the distribution they were trained on. You will design the training recipes, environments, and evaluations that tell us whether a model has truly learned a skill or has only fitted its training tasks, and turn what works into the recipes behind our production models. You will work closely with the post-training data infrastructure, evaluation, and pre-training teams.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design, run, and analyse large-scale RL post-training experiments (e.g., RLHF, RL from verifiable rewards).

 - Research and develop methods that improve out-of-distribution generalization, such as reward design, environment and task diversity, curricula, and regularization.

 - Build held-out evaluations that measure generalization to unseen tasks, domains, and formats, and that catch reward hacking and benchmark overfitting.

 - Diagnose training dynamics and failure modes, including instability, reward over-optimization, and capability regressions.

 - Turn successful research into robust, reproducible training recipes for production models.

Qualifications

 - Strong research and software engineering skills, with hands-on experience training LLMs.

 - Experience applying reinforcement learning to LLMs (e.g., PPO, GRPO, RLHF, RLVR), ideally at scale.

 - Track record of work on generalization, robustness, or distribution shift, through publications or shipped models.

 - Rigorous experimental practice: clean ablations, careful controls, and sound conclusions from noisy results.

 - Experience with distributed training (e.g., JAX, PyTorch, FSDP, Megatron) is a plus.

 - Excellent communication skills.

 - Deep understanding of data quality principles and best practices: demonstrates willingness to dive deep into data while possessing strong intuition for assessing the quality of datasets and anticipating how different data characteristics will impact model training outcomes.
   

Working Location
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

 

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   

HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

ROLE

Cerebras is looking for an AI Data Center Infrastructure Engineer to turn cluster architecture into precise, deployment-ready infrastructure designs.

You will own the critical step between a high-level system design and its implementation in a real data center. This includes defining rack layouts, equipment placement, bills of materials, power requirements, and port and cable mappings for compute, network, and storage systems.

Every deployment presents different constraints. You will adapt reference designs to the available space, power, cooling, connectivity, hardware, and logistics while preserving system performance, reliability, scalability, and serviceability.

You will also help automate this work. By building tools, validation checks, and reusable design frameworks, you will make each deployment faster, more accurate, and easier to operate at scale.

This role is well suited to an engineer who enjoys detailed systems work, practical problem-solving, and collaborating across hardware, networking, software, and data center operations.

RESPONSIBILITIES 

 - Translate cluster architectures and technical requirements into complete, deployment-ready infrastructure designs.

 - Produce and maintain rack elevations, equipment layouts, bills of materials, power allocations, port maps, and cable maps.

 - Adapt reference designs to site-specific constraints involving space, power, cooling, network connectivity, logistics, and hardware availability.

 - Validate that compute, storage, networking, power, and cabling designs work together as an integrated system.

 - Evaluate design trade-offs and recommend practical solutions that balance performance, reliability, scalability, cost, serviceability, and deployment schedule.

 - Partner with systems, network, hardware, manufacturing, supply-chain, and data center operations teams throughout the design and deployment process.

 - Participate in design and deployment-readiness reviews, identifying risks, inconsistencies, and missing requirements before installation begins.

 - Support deployment teams by resolving physical integration issues and documenting approved design changes.

 - Contribute to root-cause analysis when deployment or integration problems occur, and incorporate lessons learned into future designs.

 - Develop scripts and tools that automate design generation, BOM creation, cable mapping, consistency checks, and other repeatable workflows.

 - Improve templates, standards, documentation, and design processes so deployments become increasingly repeatable and scalable.

QUALIFICATIONS 

 - A bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related discipline—or equivalent practical experience.

 - One or more years of relevant experience in infrastructure engineering, data center design, systems integration, hardware deployment, or a related field.

 - Experience creating or working with rack elevations, equipment layouts, bills of materials, port maps, or cable maps.

 - A practical understanding of server, storage, and networking hardware and how these systems are physically integrated.

 - Familiarity with data center power, cooling, space, cabling, and serviceability constraints.

 - Experience using Python, Bash, PowerShell, or another language to automate technical workflows.

 - Strong analytical skills and close attention to detail.

 - The ability to turn incomplete or changing requirements into clear, actionable designs.

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to collaborate across several engineering disciplines.
   
   

HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

The following experience is valuable but not required:

 - Designing or deploying high-density AI, HPC, or large-scale compute clusters.

Location: Remote | Canada
Reports To: Grace Barbosa-Chin, Senior Director, P&C https://www.linkedin.com/in/grace-barbosa-chin-2212551b4/
Type: Permanent | Full-Time

Vacancy Status: This is an active, approved role and we are currently hiring for this position.

ABOUT SOLINK

Trusted by over 35,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

THE ROLE

We are looking for an AI Enablement Lead to help build and scale how our organization works with AI. This role sits within People & Culture because our opportunity with AI is fundamentally about people, capability, and how work gets done. The AI Enablement Lead will be responsible for building the skills, habits, systems, and community that enable employees to use AI effectively, responsibly, and consistently across the company.

This is not an AI engineering role. Instead, this person will operate at the intersection of AI, learning, organizational change, and business transformation. A core part of the role will be building and leading our AI Superteam: a cross-functional network of AI experts and champions embedded within each department. These individuals will maintain their existing functional reporting lines while having a dotted-line relationship to the AI Enablement Lead. Together, this network will identify opportunities, test new ways of working, share best practices, and scale high-impact AI use cases across the organization.

The ideal candidate is both AI-fluent and highly people-oriented. They do not need to be the deepest technical AI expert in the company. They need to understand what AI can enable, translate that into practical changes in how people work, and bring people together to make those changes stick.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

AI ENABLEMENT STRATEGY

 - Develop and execute a company-wide strategy for AI capability, adoption, and enablement in partnership with leadership, Technology, Security, Legal, and business teams.

 - Identify the skills, behaviours, and ways of working employees will need as AI becomes increasingly embedded in our work.

 - Build a practical roadmap for moving the organization from AI awareness to meaningful adoption and measurable impact.

AI SUPERTEAM

 - Build, coordinate, and lead a cross-functional AI Superteam made up of designated AI experts from across the organization.

 - Establish a clear operating model, expectations, priorities, and cadence for the Superteam.

 - Create a forum where teams can share experiments, successful use cases, challenges, and emerging AI practices.

 - Partner with department AI experts to identify high-value opportunities and help move promising experiments from individual use cases into scalable organizational practices.

 - Create mechanisms for knowledge-sharing so that an AI innovation in one function can be discovered and adapted by others.

LEARNING & CAPABILITY BUILDING

 - Design and deliver role-based AI learning experiences for employees, managers, and leaders.

 - Build practical resources such as playbooks, use-case libraries, prompt frameworks, guides, workshops, and office hours.

 - Help employees develop the judgment required to evaluate AI-generated work for accuracy, quality, usefulness, completeness, and appropriate human review.

 - Develop AI learning pathways that evolve as tools and organizational needs change.

ADOPTION & CHANGE MANAGEMENT

 - Drive adoption of AI tools and new AI-enabled ways of working across the organization.

 - Partner with leaders and teams to identify where AI can meaningfully improve productivity, quality, decision-making, or employee experience.

 - Help teams move beyond experimentation toward sustainable changes in workflows and operating practices.

 - Identify and address barriers to adoption, including capability gaps, confidence, behaviour, process friction, and unclear expectations.

MEASUREMENT & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

 - Define and track meaningful measures of AI adoption, capability, and impact.

 - Assess where employees and teams are making effective use of AI and where additional enablement is required.

 - Gather feedback and insights from the AI Superteam and broader employee population to continuously improve our AI strategy and programs.

 - Share progress, learnings, and recommendations with senior leadership.

WHAT THIS ROLE DOES, AND DOES NOT, OWN

The AI Enablement Lead owns organizational AI capability and adoption.

This includes:

 - AI learning and enablement

 - AI adoption and change management

 - AI community and the AI Superteam

 - Cross-functional knowledge sharing

 - Role-based AI capability development

 - Measurement of AI readiness, adoption, and impact

 - Identification and scaling of proven AI practices

This role does not independently own:

 - AI product or software engineering

 - Enterprise AI architecture

 - Cybersecurity or data security controls

 - Legal or privacy policy

 - Technical procurement or infrastructure

The AI Enablement Lead will partner closely with the teams responsible for these areas to ensure that employee enablement and technical governance evolve together.

HOW THE AI SUPERTEAM WORKS

Each major function will designate an AI Expert / AI Champion who remains embedded within their department while maintaining a dotted-line relationship to the AI Enablement Lead.

These departmental AI experts will:

 - Identify AI opportunities within their function

 - Experiment with new tools and workflows

At Hadley Designs, we believe early learning should be joyful, screen-free, and filled with connection.

Our products are developmentally sound, emotionally engaging, and intentionally designed to help children ages 3–8 grow curious, confident, and resilient.
 We serve busy, intentional families who are tired of screens and want more meaningful ways to teach and connect with their kids. From educational posters to busy books, handwriting guides to emotional learning kits, every product is crafted with care and rooted in research.
 Our vision is bold: to become the most trusted children’s brand in the world, present in millions of homes, and passed down for generations, while reaching $100 million in annual revenue by 2030.
 Today, Hadley Designs is an approximately $25 million ecommerce brand selling across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, and other channels. We've built a strong foundation, an established customer base, and a talented team of specialists. Now, our next chapter is about building a repeatable, profitable growth engine that can take us from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 We're looking for an entrepreneurial Director of Ecommerce Growth who has helped scale ecommerce brands before and knows how to turn growth opportunities into measurable business results. Someone who can see the bigger picture, connect the dots across channels, align talented teams, and determine where to invest, what to scale, and what to stop.
 This is an opportunity to take meaningful ownership of our growth strategy, build systems that consistently generate profitable demand, and help shape the next stage of Hadley Designs.
 Role Overview 
 The Director of Ecommerce Growth is responsible for building and leading Hadley Designs' next phase of profitable growth, developing a repeatable demand generation engine that can scale our business from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 This is a hands-on growth leadership role that combines strategic thinking, financial accountability, and cross-functional execution. We're looking for someone who thinks like an entrepreneur, understands the economics of scaling an ecommerce brand, and knows how to turn promising opportunities into profitable, repeatable growth systems.
 We've built a talented team of specialists across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, creative, and affiliate marketing. The Director of Ecommerce Growth connects the dots between these functions, aligning priorities, coordinating execution, removing bottlenecks, and ensuring our investments translate into measurable business results.
 This person doesn't need to be the best specialist in every channel, but they must know how to lead specialists, challenge assumptions, diagnose performance, and make the entire growth engine more effective. They take ownership of growth initiatives from strategy through execution, without relying on the CEO to drive every decision.
 The role is channel agnostic. We don't care whether our next major growth opportunity comes from Meta advertising, Amazon external traffic, Shopify, TikTok Shop, creator partnerships, AI-powered content, or an entirely new channel. What matters is identifying where the greatest opportunities exist, validating them through disciplined experimentation, and allocating resources toward what produces profitable, incremental growth.
 Equally important is knowing what not to pursue. The Director of Ecommerce Growth must be willing to challenge existing strategies, stop underperforming initiatives, and redirect resources toward higher potential opportunities.

About the role: 
 Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank. 
 Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.
 This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit. 
 Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.
 What you’ll do: 
 Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.
 Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.
 Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.
 Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.
 Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.
 Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.
 Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.
 Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.
 Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.
 Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.
 Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.
 Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.
 Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.
 Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.
 What we’re looking for: 
 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development, quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.
 Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred. 
 Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.
 Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.
 Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.
 Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.
 Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.
 High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.
 Preferred qualifications: 
 Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.
 Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.
 Knowledge of Haskell
 What success looks like: 
 Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.
 Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.
 Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.
 Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.
 Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.

Nous sommes Paramount Commerce, une entreprise canadienne de premier plan dans le domaine des technologies financières qui simplifie les paiements depuis le début des années 2000.  Alors que nous nous développons au-delà de nos marchés historiques principaux, nous faisons notre entrée dans de nouveaux marchés commerciaux à forte croissance. Afin de maintenir cette dynamique de croissance et de libérer de la capacité décisionnelle au sein de l'organisation commerciale globale, nous créons un poste de direction stratégique dédié afin de piloter, développer et commercialiser nos occasions dans les nouveaux marchés verticaux au Canada et à l'international.

 Le ou la chef des nouveaux marchés verticaux et de la croissance stratégique agira à titre de responsable exécutif(ve) et de bâtisseur(se) d'affaires, responsable de faire passer les stratégies de nouveaux marchés verticaux de l'identification des occasions à une contribution financière significative et durable.
 Relevant directement du directeur principal des revenus (Chief Revenue Officer - CRO), ce rôle se situe à la croisée de l'exécution commerciale traditionnelle, de la définition de stratégies de haut niveau, de l'alignement produit, de la coordination interfonctionnelle et de l'exécution de la stratégie de commercialisation (GTM). Vous assumerez la responsabilité globale du développement des marchés secondaires, de l'évaluation des dynamiques de marché, de la mise en place des rythmes opérationnels et du positionnement de Paramount Commerce en tant que chef de file dans les secteurs technologiques et fintech adjacents.

You'll also write the content that moves those numbers. 
 You'll work daily with Sales, and closely with Product, Customer Success, and our external PPC and SEO partners. The scope runs from HubSpot and outbound sequences to landing pages, case studies, and campaigns. 
 You'll decide which channels get tested, which content gets made, and what gets cut. AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You're responsible for the quality of the result. 
 What we value  
 Comfort with numbers, and the discipline to check them before acting on them. 
 Writing that's clear, specific, and worth reading. 
 Owning outcomes and finishing work without being chased. 
 Understanding how the business makes money and caring about results. 
 Curiosity, and a willingness to drop an approach that isn't working. 
 The honesty to say when something isn't good enough, including your own work. 
 What you'll do  
 Build and run the demand engine  
 You'll own MQL generation for the hotel division. You'll agree with Sales on what counts as a marketing-qualified lead, set targets, and report against them every week. When the number misses, you'll know why before anyone asks. 
 Most of your week goes into running programs: outbound and nurture sequences in HubSpot, paid campaigns with our PPC partner, organic search with our SEO partner, email, and landing pages. You'll test several channels in parallel, compare cost per MQL and conversion to opportunity, and move effort toward what works. 
 Write the content that converts  
 You'll write landing pages, email sequences, sales collateral, blog posts, customer stories, case studies, and product announcements yourself. Every piece has a job in the funnel, whether that's ranking for a search term, booking a demo, or helping Sales close. You'll measure whether it does that job. 
 You'll interview hotel customers and sit in on sales calls, so the content reflects how owners, GMs, and front-desk leads talk about missed calls, lost bookings, and upsells. When a piece underperforms, you'll rewrite it or retire it. 
 Own HubSpot and marketing operations  
 You'll own HubSpot end to end, including workflows, segmentation, lead scoring, routing to Sales, and reporting. You'll set lead scoring and handoff rules with the VP of Sales & Partnerships, then adjust them as you learn which signals predict a booked demo. 
 You'll build the attribution view that shows which campaigns, channels, and content pieces contribute to pipeline, and keep the data clean enough for that view to be trusted. If a dashboard says something surprising, you'll investigate before you report it. 
 What you'll bring  
 At least 3 years of hands-on experience in B2B demand generation, content marketing, or performance marketing. 
 You've owned an MQL or pipeline target and can walk us through the numbers behind it. 
 A portfolio of content you wrote yourself, such as landing pages, sequences, case studies, or articles, with results you can point to. 
 Hands-on experience with HubSpot or a similar platform, including workflows, lead scoring, and reporting. 
 You've built and run outbound or nurture sequences yourself.

 Experience working with external partners such as PPC or SEO agencies. 
 You use AI tools to move faster in research, writing, analysis, and automation, and you check what they produce. 
 You can work independently, turn a loose objective into a plan, and see it through.

 Marketing attribution models 
 Hospitality technology, hotels, or travel 
 B2B SaaS or AI products 
 Video or design skills for campaign creative 
 Trade show and event marketing 
 Building a marketing function from scratch
 An engineering, data, or other technical background 
 Why you’ll love working at Sadie

 You’ll have a lot of autonomy and visibility across both the hotel and restaurant verticals.
 There are clear growth paths: Senior Content Manager, Demand Generation Manager, or Marketing Operations.

Sales Development Representative (SDR / Setter) 
 Location: Remote
 Team: Limitless Agency, Sales
 Employment Type: Full-time, full calendar
 Base Pay: $1,000 USD per month
 Inbound Commission: 2% of cash collected on inbound appointments you set that close
 Outbound Commission: 5% of cash collected on outbound appointments you set that close
 On-Target Earnings (OTE) Range for Solid Performer: $65,760–$136,800 per year, depending on performance
 Top Performer Potential: $140,000+ per year, no cap on earnings.
 Average Deal Size: $16,000, with higher-tier packages at $30,000+.
 Lead Flow: Some inbound qualifying (triage) calls from our paid ads, plus some outbound outreach to leads who have opted in through our paid ads. The goal is to make sure our closers have full calendars of qualified appointments.
 Monthly Goal: 20 inbound deals closed from your sets + at least 5 outbound deals closed from your sets
 Time Split: The split between inbound qualifying (triage) and outbound outreach will depend on your skillset and what is a higher priority need for the team.
 Career Path: You can increase your income ceiling through performance, plus setters who prove themselves as top performers over extended periods of time may earn opportunities in either setter leadership or closing.
 We’re looking for high-performing setters who know how to turn conversations into qualified opportunities.
 You’ll work with inbound leads generated from $100k/month+ in paid advertising spend, qualify business owners, book high-ticket sales calls, and proactively create additional opportunities through outbound prospecting.
 With a $16,000 average deal size, a $1,000 monthly base, and uncapped commissions, this role offers significant earning potential for setters who consistently deliver qualified appointments that turn into closed revenue.
 About Limitless Agency 
 Limitless Agency helps digital marketing agency owners build businesses that scale and sell. Our core program, Limitless Black Card, combines one-on-one strategy with the founders, implementation support, weekly group coaching, a dedicated account team, and in-person sessions at our Tampa headquarters.
 We’ve worked with hundreds of agency owners and helped many reach six-figure monthly revenue.
 We spend well over six figures a month on paid acquisition, our sales team currently closes 25 to 50 high-ticket deals per month, and we're in the process of scaling.
 Your job is to make sure the right prospects reach our closers, keep the pipeline moving, and turn lead flow into real sales opportunities.
 Website: https://limitlessagency.io/ 
 The Opportunity 
 This isn’t a traditional appointment-setting role where success means filling a calendar with anyone willing to book.
 You’ll speak directly with agency owners and business decision-makers, understand their challenges, qualify their readiness to invest, and determine whether they’re a strong fit for our high-ticket programs.
 Most inbound prospects come from cold paid traffic. They may have only recently discovered Limitless, so you’ll need to establish trust quickly, communicate value clearly, and guide meaningful qualification conversations.
 Some of your time will be spent qualifying inbound leads, and some will be spent outbound prospecting, including reactivating inactive leads, recovering missed opportunities, and creating new conversations.
 Every qualified appointment that converts into a paying client can generate commission for you.
 At our $16,000 average deal size:
 An inbound appointment that closes generates $320 in commission.
 An outbound appointment that closes generates $800 in commission.
 Hit the monthly target of 20 inbound closes and 5 outbound closes, and your projected earnings reach $11,400 per month, or $136,800 annualized.
 Higher deal value and stronger production can increase your earnings further.
 The Role 
 We’re hiring a full-time Sales Development Representative (SDR/Setter) who can confidently manage both inbound qualification and outbound prospecting.
 Your primary responsibility is to protect our closers’ time by ensuring that only qualified, genuinely interested, and sales-ready prospects reach their calendars.
 You’ll need to move quickly, ask strong discovery questions, handle initial objections, identify buying readiness, and maintain disciplined follow-up.
 This role requires more than booking appointments. We expect you to understand what makes a prospect qualified, recognize when someone isn’t ready, and take ownership of the quality of the opportunities you generate.
 We provide the lead flow, sales process, and opportunity to grow. Your responsibility is to execute consistently and produce measurable results.
 What You’ll Do 
 Respond quickly to inbound leads generated through paid advertising.
 Lead substantive qualification conversations with agency owners and decision-makers.
 Ask effective discovery questions to understand business challenges, goals, budget, urgency, and buying readiness.
 Handle initial objections confidently and communicate the value of our offer.
 Book qualified prospects directly onto our closers’ calendars.
 Identify and remove unqualified or disengaged prospects from the calendar.
 Effectively set from outbound prospecting, pipeline reactivation, and follow-up.
 Recover inactive leads, missed appointments, and previously interested prospects.
 Personally confirm appointments 24 hours and 2 hours before their scheduled calls.
 Work closely with closers to improve appointment quality, attendance, and conversion.
 Maintain accurate pipeline stages, notes, and follow-up activities in GoHighLevel.
 Review your performance, accept coaching, and continuously improve your numbers.
 Speed to Lead & Follow-Up 
 Speed and consistency are essential to success in this role.
 We expect every setter to respond quickly, stay on top of their pipeline, and take personal responsibility for the appointments they generate.
 Our operating standards include:
 Meet the company’s speed-to-lead requirements on every applicable inbound lead.
 Personally contact every scheduled prospect 24 hours before their appointment.
 Contact them again 2 hours before the call.
 Conduct a genuine qualification conversation before booking.
 Keep accurate and updated CRM records in GoHighLevel.
 Proactively follow up on leads that haven’t responded or completed the booking process.
 Meeting the required speed-to-lead standard is required to earn and keep a spot on the team.
 What Success Looks Like 
 We measure performance based on the quality of opportunities generated and the revenue those opportunities produce, not simply the number of appointments booked.
 Monthly performance targets:
 Inbound production: 20 closed deals generated from your inbound appointments.
 Outbound production: At least 5 closed deals generated from your outbound appointments.
 Speed to lead: Consistent compliance with company standards.
 Appointment confirmations: 24-hour and 2-hour follow-up on 100% of your scheduled appointments.
 Calendar quality: Only qualified, sales-ready prospects reach the closers.
 Show rate: Strong, consistent attendance on scheduled sales calls.
 CRM discipline: Accurate records and proactive pipeline management.
 We expect high standards, accountability, and a willingness to improve continuously.
 How Compensation Works 
 This position offers a $1,000 monthly base plus uncapped commissions.
 Commissions are calculated on cash collected.
 Some clients pay in full, while others use payment plans. When clients pay over time, commissions are earned as the corresponding payments are collected, subject to the applicable commission terms.
 Commission per deal:
 $16,000 inbound deal: $320 at 2%.
 $16,000 outbound deal: $800 at 5%.
 $25,000 inbound deal: $500 at 2%.
 $25,000 outbound deal: $1,250 at 5%.
 There is no commission cap.
 Earning Potential 
 Your earnings depend on the number of appointments you generate that convert into paying clients, deal values, and cash collected.
 The following examples use our $16,000 average deal size and assume the relevant deal amounts are collected in full. They are illustrations, not guaranteed earnings.
 Lower Production — Approximately $65,760/year: 9 inbound deals and 2 outbound deals closed from your appointments. $1,000 base + $2,880 inbound commissions + $1,600 outbound commissions = $5,480/month ($65,760 annualized).
 Ramp Example — $86,880/year annualized: 12 inbound deals and 3 outbound deals closed from your appointments. $1,000 base + $3,840 inbound commissions + $2,400 outbound commissions = $7,240/month ($86,880 annualized).
 On Target — $136,800/year: 20 inbound deals and 5 outbound deals closed from your appointments. $1,000 base + $6,400 inbound commissions + $4,000 outbound commissions = $11,400/month ($136,800 annualized).
 Elite Performer — $186,720/year annualized: 28 inbound deals and 7 outbound deals closed from your appointments. $1,000 base + $8,960 inbound commissions + $5,600 outbound commissions = $15,560/month ($186,720 annualized).
 There is no cap on what you can earn.
 Important: Annual figures are annualized illustrations based on maintaining the stated monthly production. Actual earnings may vary, particularly during the initial ramp-up period and when client payments are collected over time.
 Who Thrives Here 
 This role is for someone who is competitive, highly organized, coachable, and genuinely motivated by performance-based compensation.
 You’re comfortable speaking with business owners, asking direct questions, challenging objections, and guiding conversations toward a clear next step.
 You understand that a qualified appointment is more valuable than an unqualified booking.
 You follow up without being reminded, take ownership of your pipeline, and don’t let leads sit unanswered.
 If you want a passive appointment-setting position, struggle with fast-paced environments, or need constant supervision to stay organized, this won’t be the right fit.
 Non-Negotiable Requirements 
 We’re looking for high-performing sales professionals who can demonstrate real appointment-setting or high-ticket sales experience.
 Proven experience in appointment setting, business development, or high-ticket sales over the phone.
 Experience handling inbound lead qualification and outbound prospecting, with the ability to perform both responsibilities.
 Confidence leading substantive discovery conversations with business owners or decision-makers.
 Ability to qualify prospects based on business needs, buying readiness, and fit.
 Strong initial objection-handling and consultative communication skills.
 A track record of generating qualified appointments and contributing to closed revenue.
 Strong follow-up discipline, CRM organization, and pipeline management.
 Comfort with high lead volume, performance targets, and a fast-moving sales environment.
 Availability to work full-time and maintain a consistent sales schedule.
 Willingness to receive coaching, review performance, and continuously improve.
 Experience in both inbound and outbound is strongly preferred, but candidates with exceptional experience in one area may be considered if they demonstrate the ability to succeed in the other.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience setting appointments for $10,000+ offers.
 Previous experience in B2B sales, digital marketing, agencies, consulting, or coaching programs.
 Experience with GoHighLevel.
 Experience working with leads from cold traffic.
 Experience consistently meeting or exceeding appointment-setting, show-rate, or revenue targets.
 Full-Time Commitment 
 This is a full-time role that requires consistent availability, responsiveness, and ownership of your assigned pipeline.
 We expect you to prioritize your responsibilities at Limitless Agency and maintain the availability necessary to meet the team’s performance and follow-up standards.
 Any outside commitments must not interfere with your ability to perform the role.
 Prove It 
 We’re interested in demonstrated results, not just impressive sales claims.
 Finalists may be asked to provide evidence of previous performance, such as:
 CRM screenshots or reports showing appointments booked, attendance rates, and resulting closed deals.
 Historical appointment-setting or sales performance dashboards.
 Examples of personal monthly KPIs and quota attainment.
 Recorded qualification or sales calls, where sharing is authorized.
 References from previous sales managers or business owners.
 We want to understand what you personally achieved, rather than relying solely on team-wide performance numbers.
 Base plus uncapped commission: $1,000 monthly base plus commissions on qualifying cash collected.
 Significant earning potential: $136,800 annualized at goal, with top-performer scenarios exceeding $185,000.
 Higher commissions for outbound production: Earn 5% on outbound appointments that result in closed deals.
 Consistent inbound lead flow: Substantial monthly paid advertising investment supports a growing sales operation.
 High-ticket offers: $16,000 average deal size, with higher-tier packages at $30,000+.
 Career progression: Top performers increase their earnings and may open other opportunities within Limitless.
 Sales coaching and development: Get elite-level coaching from our team and learn from experienced closers.
 100% remote: Work remotely as part of a performance-driven sales team.

We are hiring a Marketing Technology Lead to own Lyft's B2B marketing technology stack, spanning marketing automation, content and web, lead routing, data enrichment, and attribution. As the senior technical owner of that stack, you will lead solution design, own the architecture and data model that carry a lead from first touch through to a qualified opportunity, and partner with Marketing Operations, Sales Operations, Sales Technology, Privacy, Legal, and Data to translate business needs into durable, scalable systems. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who knows B2B marketing operations, can build the systems that run them, and is looking for ways to bring AI into how the stack works, not just what it produces.
 Responsibilities: 
 Serve as the senior technical owner of the B2B marketing technology stack, from solution design through delivery, adoption, and ongoing support.
 Lead requirements gathering with Marketing Operations, Sales Operations, Sales Technology, and Data partners, and translate them into functional and technical designs.
 Remain hands-on, configuring and extending the marketing automation platform (HubSpot) across workflows, forms, lead scoring, and custom objects, and building the integrations that connect the stack.
 Own the marketing technology roadmap and architecture, including the lead and account data model, enrichment and routing logic, and integrations with the CRM, data platform, web, and advertising systems.
 Own the tracking and instrumentation layer, including tag management, site and campaign tracking, and the data capture behind attribution.
 Own the lead lifecycle systems, partnering with Sales Operations and Sales Technology on lead identity, deduplication, scoring, routing, MQL and SQL definitions, and funnel stage integrity.
 Identify where AI can improve the stack, from lead scoring and routing to content and campaign workflows, and lead the evaluation, adoption, and rollout of those capabilities.
 Assess the stack against target state and introduce new tools as the marketing motion matures.
 Set the technical standard through design review and documentation that accounts for failure states, scalability, and supportability.
 Maintain platform reliability by monitoring performance and email deliverability, supporting incident resolution, leading postmortems, and driving automation.
 Own governance and controls for marketing data, including consent and subscription management, email and privacy compliance, data quality, and change management.
 Own the marketing tool portfolio and budget, from evaluation and selection through procurement, contracting, and renewals, partnering with Procurement, Legal, and Security.
 Serve as the technical expert and escalation point, and deliver technical enablement to partner teams.
 Partner with marketing leaders on prioritization, mentor the engineers and contractors supporting the stack, and support hiring.
 Communicate marketing technology strategy, roadmap, and vision to partner teams, and give senior leadership decision-ready updates on progress, risks, and tradeoffs.
 Experience: 
 Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
 7+ years of experience in a marketing technology, marketing operations engineering, or business systems role, including 3+ years leading solution design and delivery.
 5+ years of hands-on administration and configuration of a B2B marketing automation platform (HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, or Eloqua), with at least one active platform certification.
 Hands-on depth in at least two platform categories beyond marketing automation, such as content management, lead routing, data enrichment, ABM, analytics, or attribution.
 3+ years hands-on in Salesforce or an equivalent CRM, and 3 or more delivered integrations to systems such as a data warehouse or CMS using REST APIs, webhooks, or middleware.
 Hands-on experience with tag management and web or campaign tracking instrumentation.
 Led end-to-end delivery of at least 2 large, cross-functional marketing technology programs, including one platform implementation or migration.
 Experience providing technical direction to engineers, contractors, or implementation partners.
 Strong understanding of B2B demand generation and lead-to-opportunity workflows, including lead scoring, routing, attribution, and funnel reporting.
 Proven ability to communicate technical direction and tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders, and present roadmap and status to senior leadership.
 Experience with marketing data quality, consent and subscription management, and email and privacy compliance (CAN-SPAM, CASL, GDPR, or equivalent) is highly desirable.
 Experience with a cloud data platform such as Databricks or Snowflake, and with SQL, is a plus.

 Mental health benefits
 Family building benefits
 Child care and pet benefits
 Subsidized commuter benefits and Lyft ride credits

L’Expérience Aviva 
 Individuellement, nous sommes des personnes, mais ensemble, nous formons Aviva. Ces mots prennent tout leur sens lorsqu’ils deviennent nos valeurs : Bienveillance, Engagement, Collectivité et Confiance .
 À Aviva Canada, nous plaçons les gens au premier plan : nos employés, nos clients et nos collectivités. Nous sommes fiers d’une culture fondée sur la bienveillance, l’inclusion et la collaboration, où votre voix compte et votre développement est soutenu. Nous ne faisons pas que de l’assurance; nous faisons une réelle différence en protégeant ce qui compte le plus.
 L’Opportunité 
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’un chef de produit pour prendre en charge l’évolution et l’optimisation des parcours numériques offerts aux clients après l’achat — qu’il s’agisse des solutions en libre-service, du traitement des demandes d’indemnité ou de l’engagement soutenu par la télématique.
 Si vous souhaitez occuper un rôle où vous pourrez lancer des projets, expérimenter et améliorer concrètement la manière dont les clients interagissent avec nous au quotidien, ce poste est pour vous. En revanche, si vous souhaitez gérer un carnet de commandes, ce n’est pas le rôle qui vous convient.
 Ce que vous ferez: 
 Vous n’êtes pas là pour coordonner le travail, mais pour livrer des solutions concrètes et générer un véritable élan.
 On s’attendra à ce que vous exploitiez l’intelligence artificielle et des outils modernes de gestion de produit pour accélérer la mise en production — et non vous limiter à la rédaction de billets.
 Vous travaillerez sur des parcours clients en production, à fort volume, avec un impact direct et immédiat.
 Vous évoluerez au sein d’une équipe des produits pleinement intégrée, tout en bénéficiant d’un haut degré de responsabilité et d’autonomie.
 Développement (responsabilité clé) 
 Vous devrez :
 Transformer des idées, du concept au prototype fonctionnel, à l’aide d’outils d’intelligence artificielle, et déployer de façon autonome des tests A/B au moyen de plateformes d’expérimentation.
 Concevoir, tester et déployer rapidement des améliorations au sein des parcours de libre-service et d’indemnisation.
 Exemples de la façon dont on s’attend à ce que vous travailliez :  
 Utiliser l’IA générative pour concevoir des solutions, du contenu et des expérimentations.
 Tirer parti des données analytiques et de l’IA pour repérer les points de friction, les abandons de parcours et les occasions d’amélioration.
 Déployer rapidement des améliorations aux parcours (flux, messages, mécanismes d’incitation, fonctionnalités) et les faire évoluer en continu.
 Mener des tests rapides sur l’ensemble des points de contact numériques, sans alourdir les processus.
 Si votre premier réflexe est de lancer Jira, vous risquez d’éprouver des difficultés dans ce rôle.
 Prise en charge des parcours clients 
 Définir et piloter la stratégie produit ainsi que la feuille de route pour les parcours de libre-service, d’indemnisation ou liés à la télématique.
 Améliorer l’engagement client, la fidélisation et l’adoption du numérique.
 Concevoir et livrer des solutions qui simplifient les démarches des clients et maintiennent leur engagement après l’achat.
 Assurer la livraison 
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d’ingénierie, de conception et de données pour livrer des améliorations concrètes et pertinentes.
 Privilégier l’impact plutôt que le volume — se concentrer sur ce qui améliore réellement l’expérience client et la performance de l’entreprise.
 Trouver un équilibre entre les améliorations au quotidien et l’évolution du produit à plus long terme.
 On élève nos standards dans notre façon de travailler 
 Simplifier la manière dont le travail est réalisé — éliminer les processus qui freinent la livraison.
 Introduire de meilleures façons de travailler grâce à l’IA et à l’automatisation.
 Instaurer une culture axée sur la livraison, l’apprentissage et l’amélioration continue.
 Ce que vous apporterez: 
 Vous êtes orienté vers l’action 
 Vous avez déjà contribué concrètement à livrer des produits ou des fonctionnalités.
 Vous intervenez directement avec des outils et des façons de faire concrètes.
 L’IA fait partie intégrante de votre façon de travailler 
 Vous utilisez activement des outils d’IA pour gagner en efficacité.
 Vous utilisez l’IA pour réduire les dépendances et livrer plus rapidement.
 Vous avez un bon jugement produit 
 Vous savez ce qui compte vraiment… et ce qui compte moins.
 Vous misez sur l’impact plutôt que sur l’exhaustivité.
 Vous êtes capable d’avancer dans l’ambiguïté tout en livrant 
 Vous n’avez pas besoin d’un cadre parfaitement défini pour passer à l’action.
 Vous clarifiez les choses par l’action.
 Ce qui vous démarquera 
 Expérience liée aux comptes clients, à l’indemnisation ou au parcours après l’achat.
 Expérience en expérimentation, en incitations comportementales ou en mécanismes d’engagement.
 Expérience en mobilité, en télématique ou avec des solutions axées sur les données.
 Ce qu’on veut atteindre d’ici 12 à 18 mois 
 Les clients choisissent le libre-service numérique parce que c’est l’option la plus simple et la plus rapide.
 Les parcours de réclamation et de service évoluent en continu, plutôt que par livraisons ponctuelles.
 Une part importante des améliorations se fait rapidement, sans dépendances multiples.
 L’équipe travaille plus rapidement grâce aux nouvelles pratiques appuyées par l’IA que vous mettez en place.
 Bilinguisme : La connaissance de l’anglais en sus du français est exigée aux fins de communication, verbalement et par écrit, avec nos clients, nos partenaires et les équipes d’Aviva réparties à l’échelle du Canada. 
 Ce que vous gagnerez: 
 Un programme de rémunération complet comprenant le salaire de base, l’admissibilité à une prime annuelle, un régime d’épargne-retraite, un plan d’actionnariat, des avantages santé, des initiatives de bien-être et des occasions de bénévolat.
 Un modèle de travail hybride et flexible.
 Des occasions exceptionnelles de développement de carrière.
 Un régime de vacances compétitif, avec la possibilité d’acheter 5 jours supplémentaires par année.
 Des programmes dirigés par les employés, axés sur le genre, la communauté LGBTQ+, les origines, la diversité et l’inclusion.
 Des programmes de bien-être en entreprise pour soutenir la santé physique et mentale de nos employés.
 Cette offre d'emploi concerne un poste vacant existant qui a été affiché à la fois à l’interne et à l’externe.

Si vous avez un handicap qui nécessite que des mesures d’adaptation soient prises durant l'entrevue ou le processus le recrutement, veuillez communiquer avec votre partenaire de l’équipe Acquisition de talents à Aviva afin que les mesures appropriées puissent être prises.

The incumbent is responsible for securing, maintaining, and protecting the spectrum and orbital rights required to support Telesat's GSO and NGSO satellite systems. The role leads complex spectrum engineering, ITU filing and coordination activities; conducts interference and compatibility analyses; supports satellite system design from a spectrum and regulatory perspective; and represents Telesat in technical coordination discussions with satellite operators, administrations, and relevant domestic and international regulatory bodies. The position provides technical and regulatory advice that informs satellite system design, spectrum strategy, and regulatory decisions.

Main Responsibilities: Prepare, submit, and manage ITU satellite network and system filings and associated technical and regulatory showings in accordance with the ITU Radio Regulations, including applicable coordination and notification procedures.
 Collaborate with systems engineering, legal, business development, and other internal stakeholders to ensure satellite system designs and deployment plans are consistent with applicable spectrum and regulatory requirements and that associated filings accurately reflect system design and operational characteristics.
 Analyze ITU examination results and regulatory findings, determine appropriate technical and regulatory responses, and lead coordination activities with other satellite operators and administrations through to resolution.
 Perform interference, sharing, compatibility, and coordination analyses involving GSO and NGSO satellite networks and systems, other space services, and terrestrial services, including link-budget and carrier-level analyses as applicable.
 Prepare and manage domestic regulatory applications, filings, and associated technical submissions through to completion with relevant national authorities.
 Develop and support contributions to ITU-R Working Parties, relevant regional organizations and preparatory groups, and WRC processes in support of Telesat's spectrum and regulatory objectives.
 Prepare technical and regulatory analyses, coordination correspondence, briefing materials, recommendations, and presentations for internal stakeholders and senior management.
 Lead technical coordination discussions and negotiations with satellite operators and administrations and support the development and conclusion of coordination agreements.
 Provide strategic technical and regulatory advice and recommendations to senior management on spectrum access, protection, coordination, system design, and associated regulatory risks and opportunities.
Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Telecommunications, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree preferred.
 Minimum 7 years of relevant professional experience in satellite spectrum engineering, RF engineering, satellite communications, or telecommunications regulatory engineering.
 Demonstrated experience applying the ITU Radio Regulations to satellite networks and systems, particularly Articles 9 and 11 and associated Rules of Procedure.
 Demonstrated proficiency in satellite link-budget, interference, compatibility, and coordination analysis.
 Experience with relevant ITU Radiocommunication Bureau software and databases used for satellite filing and coordination activities.
 Proficiency with analytical/programming tools such as Python or MATLAB; experience with commercial satellite-system or interference-analysis tools is an asset.
 Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, including the ability to communicate complex technical and regulatory matters to technical and non-technical audiences.
 Strong analytical, organizational, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Decision Making and Supervision: The incumbent exercises substantial independent technical judgment in the development and execution of spectrum filing, coordination, and interference-analysis strategies. The incumbent develops recommendations concerning the acquisition, maintenance, and protection of spectrum and orbital rights and advises on regulatory and spectrum-related constraints that may influence satellite system design and operations. Matters involving significant commercial, legal, policy, or corporate commitments are escalated to the appropriate decision-making authority.
 The role does not currently require direct people management but may provide technical leadership, mentoring, and guidance to engineers and other team members.
Working Conditions: Position is based in Ottawa, Ontario, with a hybrid work arrangement.
 Domestic and international travel may be required to support coordination negotiations, regulatory meetings, ITU-R activities, and related industry events.
